SYNTHETIC Options playground report

10-year real-quote sample; results are relative comparisons, not forecasts.
SYNTHETIC: every number on this page comes from generated fixture logs (make-synthetic-logs), not from market data. It only proves the machinery works.

Generated 2026-10-15 03:51 from 19 run(s), 19 profile/config variants in /tmp/claude-0/s4. Research software, not advice. Start equity $100,000; idle cash earns 3.6% APY; sizing = allocation x current equity split equally across tickers; per-expiry cap 60% of a ticker's share per expiry; circuit breaker off. Monte Carlo: 3,000 paths, 2-month blocks, seed 7, horizons 12 and 36 months; bootstrap understates tails.

How to become an expert at losing money

Bootstrap of a ~10-year sample understates tails (no month worse than the worst observed can appear). P(broke) is over 36 months. Multiple = P(broke) / base P(broke), base floored at 0.1%; ties broken by P(drawdown > 50%). Missing logs show as not run.

Management-rule scorecard

8 configurations compared against baseline baseline. Saved = loss avoided vs holding to expiry; cost = gain given up; whipsaw = share of protective exits (stop, breach, trigger) that would have finished profitable. "vs baseline" is the mean per-contract P&L difference on the same entries (same ticker, strategy, entry date). A rule is "holds up" only if it beats baseline in both the first and second half of the sample; otherwise "unproven". Configs with different strikes (delta/profile variants) are not management rules and are excluded: experiment_all_off/alloff, green/delta10, green/delta25, green/delta30, green/delta35, red/d25_wide, yellow_E4/d20.

What this does NOT tell you

  • A ~10-year sample: relative comparison only, not a forecast; tails are understated.
  • Bootstrap resampling can never create a month worse than the worst one observed.
  • No taxes, no margin-call mechanics, no early-assignment modelling beyond the logged flag.
  • Unit logs are replayed at fixed sizing rules; real fills at size would differ (liquidity, slippage).
  • 10-year real-quote sample; results are relative comparisons, not forecasts.
